title: [spec-gap][R-19-025] SOS arming is not connected to the spec-18 SOS send path
description: spec/19-device-ux.md §8: SOS rides the normal send path with priority — no special radio mode exists (matches spec 18). The send-path half is implemented+tested: TX_PRIORITY_SOS=0 with preemption (lichen/subsys/lichen/link/include/lichen/tx_queue.h:61; lichen/tests/tx_queue/main.c:156,469-474 vs test/vectors/tx_queue_priority.json; python tx_queue.py). The arming half is unwired: nothing consumes LICHEN_UX_BUTTON_EVT_SOS_ARM / SOS_DEDICATED (rg consumers: zero outside tests) to enqueue an SOS alert. All sender pieces exist: sos_alert.c (CBOR, spec 18.4.2, vectors sos_cbor.json), sos_origin.c (Schnorr48 origin signature, vectors sos_signature.json), sos_ratelimit.c, TX_PRIORITY_SOS queue. Fix: an app-level handler (registered via lichen_ux_button_start) that, on SOS_ARM/SOS_DEDICATED, composes the SOS alert (CBOR + origin signature) and enqueues at TX_PRIORITY_SOS; H-tier LED already flips to SOS_ACTIVE via the button backend. Note Rust link layer has no TX queue (precedence.rs is time-source policy) — C path is the reference.
